scenes.title: TITANIC
scenes.subtitle: The Last 2 Hours 40 Minutes
scenes.narration: April the fourteenth, 1912. The largest moving object ever built by humans is racing across the North Atlantic. In less than three hours, it will be gone.
RMS Titanic was 269 metres long, the largest ship afloat. Newspapers called her practically unsinkable, because her hull was split into sixteen watertight compartments.
She left Southampton on April the tenth, stopped at Cherbourg in France and Queenstown in Ireland, then turned west for New York.

scenes.label: people on board
scenes.narration: On board were about two thousand two hundred and twenty four people, from millionaires in first class to emigrants in third class, chasing a new life.

scenes.title: Lifeboat seats vs people on board
scenes.narration: But there was a problem nobody worried about. Titanic carried twenty lifeboats, with room for only one thousand one hundred and seventy eight people. Barely half.

scenes.title: Sunday, 14 April 1912
items: Several ice warnings received by radio
scenes.narration: On Sunday, the radio room received several warnings about ice ahead. The sea was flat calm, there was no moon, and the ship kept up her speed of about twenty two knots.

scenes.label: ICEBERG RIGHT AHEAD
scenes.narration: At eleven forty that night, lookout Frederick Fleet saw a dark shape in the water and rang the bell three times. Iceberg, right ahead!
The officers turned hard and reversed the engines, but there was no time. The iceberg scraped along the starboard side, below the waterline.
Five of the sixteen compartments began to flood. Titanic could survive four. With five, the water would spill over from one to the next, like water in an ice cube tray.

scenes.text: She is going to sink. An hour, perhaps an hour and a half.
scenes.by: Thomas Andrews, the ship's designer (as recalled by survivors)
scenes.narration: Her designer, Thomas Andrews, inspected the damage and gave the captain the verdict. The ship was going to sink, and soon.
Just after midnight, the crew uncovered the lifeboats. The radio operators sent distress calls, and at about a quarter to one, the first lifeboat was lowered into the dark.

scenes.label: people in Lifeboat 1
scenes.narration: Many passengers still believed the ship was safer than a small boat on a freezing sea. So the first boats left half empty. Lifeboat one carried just twelve people.
Help was coming. The liner Carpathia heard the call about fifty eight nautical miles away, and raced north through the ice at full speed. But she needed nearly four hours.
By two in the morning, the bow was deep under water and the stern was rising into the air. The last lifeboat left at five past two.

scenes.label: TITANIC SINKS
scenes.narration: At two twenty a.m., Titanic broke apart and sank. Two hours and forty minutes after the collision.

scenes.title: In the water
items: Most people in the water died within minutes
scenes.narration: The water was about minus two degrees Celsius. Hundreds of people were in the water, and most died within minutes from the cold. Only one lifeboat went back to look for survivors.

scenes.title: When Carpathia arrived
scenes.narration: Carpathia arrived at about four in the morning. She found around seven hundred survivors in the lifeboats. More than fifteen hundred people had died.

scenes.title: What changed after Titanic
items: Lifeboat seats for everyone on board
scenes.narration: The disaster changed the sea forever. New rules required lifeboat seats for everyone, radios staffed day and night, and an ice patrol that still watches the North Atlantic today.

scenes.compare: About 4.5 times the height of the world's tallest building
scenes.narration: In 1985, explorers finally found the wreck, almost four kilometres down, broken in two, exactly as some survivors had described.

scenes.title: TITANIC
scenes.narration: Titanic was built to be unsinkable. In the end, it was the ship that taught the world that nothing is. Follow GetYr Studio for more stories from history.
